record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: For a metric continuum, where CDH means that any two countable dense subsets can be carried onto each other by a self-homeomorphism, is every CDH metric continuum strongly locally homogeneous (SLH)?

evidence.quote: An important special case of Problem 1 remains unsolved.
Problem 1’. Is every CDH metric continuum SLH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A separable space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $f \colon X \to X$ with $f(D) = E$. A space $X$ is strongly locally homogeneous (SLH) if it has an open base $\mathcal{B}$ such that for every $B \in \mathcal{B}$ and any two points $x, y \in B$ there is a homeomorphism $f \colon X \to X$ with $f(x) = y$ and $f$ equal to the identity outside $B$. A metric continuum is a compact, connected, metrizable space with more than one point.

It is known (Bessaga–Pełczyński) that every SLH Polish space is CDH. 

Question. Is every CDH metric continuum strongly locally homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and recent papers on countable dense homogeneity describe the relationship between CDH and SLH for Polish/continuum settings as a delicate, still-open problem; no resolution showing every CDH metric continuum is SLH (or producing a counterexample) was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of CDH vs SLH; the question whether there is a Polish space SLH but not CDH (and related implications) treated as open/delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) survey-style paper still treats relations between CDH and SLH as open.

status_evidence.title: Ungar's theorems on countable dense homogeneity revisited (van Mill)
status_evidence.snippet: Every SLH Polish space is CDH (Bessaga–Pełczyński); converse problems remain.
status_evidence.claim: Standard implication SLH ⇒ CDH established; reverse direction for continua not established.
